title: SKCapstone CardStore evidence event (coordination/card_events)
description:
The EVIDENCE half of the two-store split. Structure lives in cards/<id>/events/*.jsonl and keys its type as 'action'; this store also uses 'action' but carries link/label facts rather than lifecycle. Neither store alone answers whether a card is done AND passed.

ORDERING: 'seq' is PER WRITER FILE, not global. Measured: 145 of 145 multi-writer cards have two or more files both starting at seq 0. Cross-writer ordering MUST use ts, then writer, then event_id. Ordering by seq silently interleaves history wrong.

seq.description: Per-writer-file counter. NEVER valid for cross-writer ordering.

link_key.description:
Either a canonical core key (see evidence_vocab.CORE, 61 keys) or the namespaced escape form x-<agent>-<key>. Lowercase, underscore-separated. A timestamp or hash in the KEY is rejected: it belongs in the value. Live data has 125 keys with a timestamp baked in, e.g. verdict-20260826T021646Z, which makes every such event invisible to a reader asking for 'verdict'.

WHY CONTROLLED: 19408 link events currently use 3674 distinct keys; the top 100 cover 49 percent. human_approval alone has 26 spellings, so a safety check reading only the canonical key finds 41 of 173 recorded approvals. Supersession has 14 spellings, which is why a card was once ranked highest-leverage while actually superseded twice.
